==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰuH-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|future}}, {{m|enm|futur}}, from {{der|en|fro|futur}}, from {{der|en|la|futūrus}}, irregular future active participle of {{m|la|sum||to be}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰuH-||to become, be}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|bēo||to become, will be; to be}}. More at {{l|en|be}}. {{doublet|en|futur}}. Displaced native {{cog|ang|tōweard}}, which took on a different meaning as {{m|en|toward}}, and {{noncog|enm|afterhede|t=future|lit=afterhood}} in the given sense.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈfjuː.t͡ʃə/|[ˈfjʊu̯.t͡ʃə]|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈfju.t͡ʃɚ/|[ˈfjʊu̯.t͡ʃɚ]|~|[ˈfjʊu̯.t͡ʃɹ̩]|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-future.wav}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-future.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːtʃə(ɹ)|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|fu|ture}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|Q344}}The [[time]] [[ahead]]; those [[moment]]s [[yet]] to be [[experience]]d.
#* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|system=PC|scene=Krogan: Culture Codex entry|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|text=This solitary attitude stems in part from a deep sense of fatalism and futility, a profound social effect of the genophage that caused krogan numbers to dwindle to a relative handful. Not only are they angry that the entire galaxy seems out to get them, the krogan are also generally pessimistic about their race's chances of survival. The surviving krogan see no point to building for the '''future'''; there will be no '''future'''. The krogan live with an attitude of "kill, pillage, and be selfish, for tomorrow we die."}}
# Something that will happen in moments yet to come.
# Goodness in what is yet to come. Something to look forward to.
#: {{ux|en|There is no '''future''' in dwelling on the past.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21582512-explosion-start-ups-changing-finance-better-revenge-nerds Revenge of the nerds]
|passage=Think of banking today and the image is of grey-suited men in towering skyscrapers. Its '''future''', however, is being shaped in converted warehouses and funky offices in San Francisco, New York and London, where bright young things in jeans and T-shirts huddle around laptops, sipping lattes or munching on free food.}}
# The likely prospects for or fate of someone or something in time to come.
# {{lb|en|grammar}} Verb tense used to talk about events that will happen in the future; [[future tense]].
# {{lb|en|finance}} {{alternative form of|en|futures}}.
# {{lb|en|computing|programming}} An [[object]] that retrieves the value of a [[promise]].
# {{lb|en|sports}} A [[minor-league]] [[prospect]].

====Usage notes====
* {{sense|finance}} The one who agrees to, at a future date, sell the commodity is considered to be selling the future; the other buys it.
* {{sense|finance}} A non-standardized contract to buy and sell in the future is called [[forward]] or [[forward contract]].

{{C|en|Future|Time}}

==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|interjeccioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|interjection}} (13th century), from {{der|en|la|interiectiōnem}}, accusative singular of {{m|la|interiectiō||throwing or placing between; interjection}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|intericiō||throw or place between}}, from {{m|la|inter||between}} + {{m|la|iaciō||throw}}. {{surf|en|interject|-ion}}. Displaced {{cog|ang|betwēoxāworpennes|lit=between-thrown-out-ness}}, a [[calque]] of the Latin.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪn.təˈdʒɛk.ʃən/|a=UK}}
* {{enPR|ĭn'tər.jĕkʹshən|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/ˌɪn.tɚˈd͡ʒɛk.ʃən/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-interjection.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|interjection.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛkʃən|s=4}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|grammar}}{{lb|en|countable|grammar}} A [[phrase#Noun|phrase]] or [[word#Noun|word]] with no [[particular#Adjective|particular]] [[grammatical]] [[relation]] to a [[sentence#Noun|sentence]] but which [[serve#Verb|serves]] to [[express#Verb|express]] [[emotion]] or as a [[filled pause]]; an [[exclamation]].
#: {{syn|en|interj<q:abbreviation>|interj.<q:abbreviation>}}
#: {{hypo|en|expletive<id:offensive interjection>}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} Something which is [[interject]]ed; an [[interruption]].
#: {{syn|en|insertion|intercalation|interpolation}}
#* {{RQ:WaPo|date=2020-01-23|author=Philip Bump|title=Mnuchin said Thunberg needed to study economics before offering climate proposals. So we talked to an economist.|text=Mnuchin, asked about climate change in a CNBC interview after his comments about Thunberg, argued there were bigger issues that also needed to be addressed. When a host noted clean air rules as an example of something that might be more urgent, Mnuchin ignored the '''interjection'''.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The act of [[interject]]ing something.
#* {{RQ:WaPo|date=9 February 1986|quotee=w:Carlo Ginzburg|title=Lives: Of Cheese, Witches, No TV And Histories of Common Men|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/opinions/1986/02/09/lives/cc1648fb-6ebd-4873-9078-6b66e6c2acb7/|passage=You can see how those people slowly interjected the inquisitors’ theme about witchcraft, about the witches’ sabbath. And how they slowly transformed their own beliefs into the witchraft beliefs. It took 50 years. I was fascinated by the possibility of reconstructing that kind of '''interjection''' – you interject a self-damaging image, a cultural pattern which is foreign to your own culture, from your enemy, from those judges.}}
#* {{RQ:NYT|date=12 February 2007|author=Cornelia Dean|title=A creationist takes a place in the world of fossils|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260000000000*/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/02/12/health/12iht-create.4568557.html|passage=If researchers like [[w:John Baumgardner|{{quote-gloss|John}} Baumgardner]] do their work “without any form of '''interjection''' of personal dogma,” {{quote-gloss|John}} Geissman said, “I would have to keep as objective a hat on as possible and say, ‘O.K., you earned what you earned.’”}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=16 January 2024|author=w:Marina Hyde|title=If {{w|Harrison Ford}} and {{w|John Travolta}} can be crowned living legends of aviation, why not {{w|Prince Harry}}?|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240116145154/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2024/jan/16/harrison-ford-john-travolta-living-legends-of-aviation-prince-harry|passage=[A]n online petition – perhaps the most ineffectual form of '''interjection''' in modern public life, even including words spoken into the void on [[w:Talk (streaming service)|TalkTV]] – states the decision to honour the Duke of Sussex is a travesty on the part of “such an esteemed organisation”.}}
#* {{RQ:NYT|date=29 April 2026|author=Ben Kenigsberg|title=Three Great Documentaries to Stream|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/29/movies/three-great-documentaries-to-stream.html|passage=The title — sometimes styled with an exclamation point: “[[w:Point of Order (film)|Point of Order!]]” — refers to one of the senator {{quote-gloss|{{w|Joseph McCarthy}}}}’s favored methods of '''interjection'''. He grandstands, he deflects, he insinuates — sometimes to the clear exasperation of his interrogators.}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|of [[viviparous]] animals}} To [[release]] [[live]] [[offspring]] from the [[body]] into the [[environment]].
#: {{ux|en|It was clear that she was about to '''give birth'''.}}

#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1988
|author=Emily Honig; w:Gail Hershatter
|chapter=Divorce
|title=Personal Voices: Chinese Women in the 1980's
|url=https://archive.org/details/personalvoicesch00honi/

Then Xu immediately began to beat Qu, and forced her and the baby to live in a small shack.}}
#* {{quote-web
|en
|date=June 1, 2022
|author=Collier Jennings
|title='{{w|The Orville}}': Everything You Need to Know Before Season 3

|work=The Collider
|text=The rest of the ''Orville's'' crew underwent changes as well. Bortus' beliefs were challenged when he '''gave birth''' to a daughter - on Moclan society, males are the dominant species and females must undergo a mandatory sex change.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260927103728/https://collider.com/orville-season-3-everything-you-need-to-know-before/|archivedate=27 September 2026}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively|usually|with ''to''|idiom}} To become the [[source]] of.
#: {{ux|en|Einstein '''gave birth''' to a famous equation relating energy to mass.}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:fynden|tree=1}}
{{inh+|en|enm|fynden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|findan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*finþan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*finþaną}}, a secondary verb from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*pent-||to go, pass; path bridge}}.

See also {{cog|fy|fine}}, {{cog|nds|finden}}, {{cog|nl|vinden}}, {{cog|de|finden}}, {{cog|da|finde}}, {{cog|nb|finne}}, {{cog|nn|-}} and {{cog|sv|finna}}; also {{cog|en|path}}, {{cog|sga|étain||I find}}, {{m|sga|áitt||place}}, {{cog|la|pōns||bridge}}, {{cog|grc|πόντος||sea}}, {{cog|xcl|հուն||ford}}, {{cog|ae|𐬞𐬀𐬧𐬙𐬃}}, {{cog|sa|पथ|tr=pathá||path}}, {{cog|sla-pro|*pǫtь}}.

For the meaning development compare {{m+|sla-pro|*najьti}} > {{m+|ru|найти́}}, akin to {{m+|sla-pro|*jьti}} > {{m|ru|идти́}}; {{m+|ru|находи́ть}}, {{m|ru|нахо́дка}}, akin to {{m|ru|ход}}, {{m|ru|ходи́ть}}.
